New note: policy gradient methods as the family that optimises the policy directly. States the policy-gradient theorem and the log-derivative identity, REINFORCE and its variance, baselines and the advantage, the actor-critic split, TRPO's KL-constrained surrogate and PPO's clipped objective with the update equations, and the deterministic (DDPG, TD3) and maximum-entropy (SAC) variants, with the table of failure modes and remedies and the trust-region reading. References the theorem paper, REINFORCE, TRPO, PPO and SAC.

New note, independent of the derivative: the finite difference as an operator and a calculus of its own. It takes the discrete calculus as primary and the derivative as its limit, and the argument is that this is not stylistic — the difference is defined on every lattice function with no convergence hypothesis, while D = (1/h) ln(1+Delta) is a series in Delta, so the dependency runs the other way. Sections: the three differences and the binomial form of the nth difference; the shift algebra (Delta = E - 1, E = exp(hD)) and the twisted Leibniz rule that carries the discreteness as a correction term; summation as the exact inverse, with no constant of integration, and the falling factorials that lower the index; Newton forward-difference formula as the discrete Taylor theorem, with the Stirling numbers conjugating powers into falling factorials and the umbral calculus as the reason identities transfer; and the uses — numerical differentiation, discretisation, difference equations, telescoping sums, generating functions. Three QA answers, including why the constant of integration is the price of the continuum rather than a feature of inversion. References: Taylor 1717 through LeVeque 2007.

Add a History of the Integral section, eight stages from Eudoxus' exhaustion to the Kurzweil-Henstock gauge integral: indivisibles and the inverse-tangent relation, the algorithms of Newton and Leibniz, Euler's integrals as functions, the Cauchy-Riemann-Darboux rigour, Stieltjes and Lebesgue and the integral as a functional, and the Volterra-Fredholm-Hilbert moment when the kernel becomes an operator. It closes with the argument for the operator reading: convolution, the Fourier and Laplace transforms, Green's functions and fractional integrals are all kernels of one kind. New note: the power series as an object rather than as a representation. Convergence first — the set of points is an interval or disc, Cauchy-Hadamard fixes the radius from the coefficients, and the boundary is undecided by the formula and decided point by point, which is where the interesting failures live. Then the two readings: inside the disc it is an analytic function (term-by-term operations, identity theorem, radius as distance to the nearest singularity), and with convergence dropped it is the formal ring R[[x]] containing R[x] as the terminating subring, where 1/(1-x) is an identity without any hypothesis and invertibility is a condition on the constant term — the setting of generating functions. A closing section keeps three distinctions the corpus needs: power series against polynomial, against the Taylor representation (coefficients fixed by derivatives of a given function), and against the general series.

Expand the polynomial taxonomy from 25 to 57 families in 12 categories: the algebraic-property group (monic, irreducible, primitive, minimal, square-free, reciprocal, cyclotomic), the completed classical orthogonal set (Chebyshev of the second kind, Zolotarev/Solotarev, Askey-Wilson), the discrete orthogonal lattice families (Hahn, Krawtchouk, Meixner, Charlier), interpolation and approximation (Bernstein, Lagrange basis, Newton), the combinatorial sequence polynomials (Fibonacci, Lucas, Pell, Abel, Bell/Touchard, Eulerian, Narayana), graph polynomials (chromatic, Tutte, independence), the coefficient-domain families (Boolean, tropical, Puiseux), and the trinomial term count. Function Representation: a new section giving the representation table — Taylor, Fourier, Laurent, power series, Chebyshev, wavelet — with its building blocks, and a subsection on the Taylor representation. New note: the Pade representation as a member of the representation family, beside Taylor. States the matching rule (blocks are ratios P_m/Q_n, coefficients fixed by reproducing the Taylor series through order m+n by a linear system), places it in the building-blocks table with Taylor, Fourier, Laurent, power series, Chebyshev and wavelet, and works the consequences: poles become first-class where a Taylor series cannot carry a singularity, the diagonal sequence continues the series in capacity, and divergent asymptotic series are resummed. Then the failure modes kept apart - spurious poles and Froissart doublets, singular matching systems and defects, no universal convergence theorem, and the conditioning of the Toeplitz system - and the distinction between representation, approximant and sequence, with the continued-fraction route. References: Pade 1892, Baker 1975, Baker & Graves-Morris 1996, Bender & Orszag 1978, Press et al. 2007 (local record), plus the corpus links.

New note: the Taylor representation as a representation in its own right, split out of the representation master because its building blocks carry their own theory. The note states the conversion (blocks are the powers of x-a, coefficients are the derivatives, so local behaviour at a point becomes a sequence), places it in the table of representations with how each one extracts its coefficients (derivatives, inner products, contour integrals, projection under a weight), and works the three consequences: local data becomes a sequence, operations become algebra on formal power series, truncation becomes an approximation governed by a remainder. Then the failure the representation hides: it represents the germ, not the function — the radius is bounded by the nearest singularity, and a smooth function like exp(-1/x^2) has the zero series at the origin, so analyticity is exactly the condition under which the representation determines its object. A section keeps the series and its truncation apart, since the polynomial is routinely called the series. References: Taylor 1717, Rudin 1976, Feigenbaum 1985, Krantz & Parks 2002, plus the corpus links and the persona.

New note: the polynomial ring as a structure rather than as an object. Filed under structure/algebra, with a directory link from cossical/ where the polynomial itself lives. The note defines R[x] as finitely supported sequences under convolution, then answers its own QA question — what "the algebraic structure" means — by showing that the operations reading (commutative ring, free R-module, graded ring, R-algebra) and the construction reading (free commutative R-algebra on one generator, with Hom_{R-Alg}(R[x],S) congruent to S) are the same description, so that every relation on x is a quotient and adjoining a root is the same operation as adjoining any element. It tabulates what R[x] inherits from R (field to Euclidean to PID to UFD; Gauss; Hilbert; the degree law and its failure under zero divisors), separates the polynomial from the polynomial function (eval is injective exactly when R is infinite; over F_p the kernel is (x^p - x)), and closes on quotients as the point of the construction. References: Kronecker 1882, Hilbert 1890, Steinitz 1910, Noether 1921 and 1927, van der Waerden 1931, Zariski-Samuel 1958, Atiyah-Macdonald 1969, Lang 2002, Dummit-Foote 2004, Cox-Little-O'Shea 2015.

New note on the Monge–Kantorovich theory: Monge’s 1781 earthworks problem and why his map can fail to exist, Kantorovich’s 1942 coupling and the linear program it becomes, Kantorovich duality and the shipper’s prices, Brenier’s gradient-of-a-convex-potential theorem, McCann’s displacement convexity and Otto’s Wasserstein geometry, the Benamou–Brenier dynamic formulation, and the Sinkhorn/Cuturi computational turn. Note created. Chemical engineering as its own discipline rather than a member of chemical sciences: the family note asks which substance and by which transformation, this one asks how that transformation is carried at industrial scale, and its warrant is a plant in specification rather than an assay that reproduces. Full Formulation with the five questions, the boundary / stopping-rule / identity / typing block, and a 121-row instance tree: orientation (industrial transformation purpose, on-specification and envelope-integrity goals, the scale-up, transport, separation, dynamics and safety-envelope gaps), agents, the segment (reaction system, transport path, separation train, flowsheet, operating envelope), observables (conversion, selectivity, space-time yield, residence-time distribution, pressure drop, purity and recovery, energy demand), access (lab reactor to pilot plant to instrumented plant, PAT, calorimetry), representation (balances, rate laws, the transport equations, PFD and P&ID, dimensionless groups, reactor, simulator, CFD and control models), evaluation, communication, infrastructure, context, guidance (conservation, rate-limiting step, unit-operation decomposition, similarity, inherent safety, recycle and purge) and fifteen member practices from reaction engineering to process intensification. Critical evaluation leads with the verdict that the warrant is local while the claim is general, grades scale-up validity and empirical warrant moderate, and closes on the limits of pilot-plant evidence and on the discipline's silence about whether a product should be made at all.

Add the maximum principle as an epistemic principle: the extremal-degeneracy theorems of potential theory and second-order PDE read as a directive about where the information is -- bound the interior by describing the boundary, transfer bounds by comparison, and treat an interior extremum as a diagnostic. States the four statements that carry the name (Hopf/Nirenberg/elliptic comparison, Hamilton's tensor form, the viscosity and discrete reformulations, and Pontryagin's homonym), grows the family as a member set because the guide licenses no part-link for a principle, shows why the sign condition and the operator order carry the result (the first eigenfunction and the biharmonic counterexample, the hyperbolic domain of dependence), and contrasts it with least action and stationarity, where the extremum is held inside the admissible set.

Retarget the Harmonic Analysis link to the discipline note and state the distinction the line was blurring: the maximum principle is stated for the harmonic functions in the kernel of the Laplacian, not for the eigenfunctions harmonic analysis decomposes.

New Variable Interaction section: the forms two variables can take in a model (additive, multiplicative, interaction in regression, exponential, Cobb-Douglas) read as a ladder of epistemic commitments about the aspects of reality - separability, jointness, context-dependence - with the exponential as the multiplicative form on the log scale and Cobb-Douglas as the elasticity case. Closes on the interpretability trap: an interaction makes the main effect the effect at Z = 0, which is why centring is the usual remedy.

Moved out of theory/ to the epistemic root. A variable is not a theory element: it is the epistemic abstraction of a dimension of variation, while the theory directory holds the conceptual apparatus (modelling, VRAT, state descriptor) that uses variables. The four inbound links were re-pointed; content unchanged apart from the Variable Interaction section.

Add Opportunity Cost as a concept of decision theory: the value of the best alternative forgone, OC(a_i) = max over j != i of V(a_j), with its four well-definedness conditions (availability, exclusivity, comparable valuation, selection) and the five essential elements (scarcity, alternatives, exclusivity, selection, forgone value). The note separates the best-forgone rule from the sum of all rejected alternatives with the government-budget example (144 -> 120, net advantage 30), bounds the concept against explicit, accounting and sunk cost and against regret, reads it as ex ante (Buchanan: cost is displaced by choice), declares the valuation rather than assuming it, and records the two failures of operationalizability: the counterfactual is unobservable, and the alternative set is a modelling choice that widening can make arbitrarily expensive.

Note created. The spectrogram as the time-frequency reading of a signal: the squared magnitude of the short-time Fourier transform, one spectrum per frame, time across and frequency down with power carried by intensity. Records the construction chain (frame, window, FFT, square, assemble) and the two quantities that follow from the parameters alone, the bin spacing f_s/N and the column spacing H/f_s, with a parameter table for sampling rate, frame length, hop, window and dB scaling. The central section is the resolution trade-off: a short frame localises a click and smears its pitch, a long frame resolves close partials and smears their onsets, bounded by the Gabor limit and restated by every window function as leakage against main-lobe width — so a spectrogram is read as a choice about which structures to resolve rather than measured. Adds a reading table (harmonics as parallel bands, vibrato as wobble, transients as vertical stripes, chirps as slopes, noise as a floor, aliasing as a fold), a variants table (linear, mel, log-frequency and constant-Q, reassigned, synchrosqueezed, scalogram), and the limits: phase discarded so reconstruction needs Griffin-Lim or the complex STFT, quasi-stationarity assumed inside each frame, leakage and scalloping, and the trade-off as the shape of the object rather than a defect. References: Wikipedia spectrogram, STFT, Gabor limit and mel scale, Allen and Rabiner 1977, Harris 1978, Griffin and Lim 1984, Oppenheim and Schafer, plus links into the signal cluster and to Frequency (Periodicity).

New essay: how the periodic table became a predictive instrument. The question (what must be true of a classification before it can predict), the near-misses before 1869 with the table of why each fell short, Mendeleev's three commitments (reorder against the weights, leave gaps, derive properties), the predicted-versus-measured table for gallium, scandium and germanium, the tellurium/iodine anomaly as the defect he accepted, Moseley's atomic number as the correction and the quantum explanation as the new foundation, the modern 118-element table, and the closing epistemic reading of the nomological taxonomy - stable ordering, periodic property, and the discipline to leave a gap.

New history note: the law of falling bodies from Aristotle's weight-proportional fall and the argument against the void, through Philoponus, Buridan's impetus and Oresme's mean-speed theorem, the Renaissance experiments of Benedetti and Stevin's Delft drop, Galileo's inclined plane, odd-number law, definition of uniform acceleration, conceptual experiment and the Pisa legend with its evidence, the measurement of g from Huygens to Kater, Newton's Moon test and universal gravitation, and the modern equivalence-principle tests. Closes with the historiographical dispute - Koyre, Drake, Settle - and the reading of the law as the case in which the modern idea of a physical law was worked out.

Add Nicotine as a substance of the molecular family: C10H14N2, a pyridine ring and a pyrrolidine ring joined by one bond with a methyl on the pyrrolidine nitrogen and a single stereocentre at C2', the natural (S)-enantiomer. The note carries the two precursors (nicotinic acid through the NAD route for the pyridine ring, ornithine through putrescine and the N-methyl-Delta1-pyrrolinium cation for the pyrrolidine) and the still-unsettled coupling between them, root synthesis and xylem transport with the grafting experiment that shows the plant is not its own target, antiherbivore neurotoxicity against Manduca sexta's counter-adaptations, alpha4-beta2 receptor affinity near 1 nM and dopaminergic reinforcement, and the attributes that fix the substance: the 8.1 and 3.4 pKa pair, membrane permeability, 247 C volatility and green tobacco sickness, optical activity, toxicity, teratogenicity, and the point the literature blurs -- nicotine is not classified as a carcinogen while the smoke carries the carcinogens, and the usual 60 mg lethal dose descends from nineteenth-century self-experiments.

New note: the arch, filed on the body shelf as an instance of Structure, not as a new root and not in technica. The curve is a path rather than a profile: the arch stands when a line of thrust can be found inside its own material for every load it must carry, and falls when none exists. It is distinguished from the beam by material requirement rather than by shape — a beam needs a material that can pull, an arch only one that can push, which is why masonry builds arches. Forms (semicircular, segmental, pointed, flat), parts (voussoir, abutment), quantities (thrust, rise, thickness) and two bounds: no tension, and the four-hinge mechanism.

New note: the beam, the member in bending. Three quantities decide it — span, second moment of area and elastic modulus — and deflection scales with the fourth power of the span, which is why a small increase in span is a large increase in depth. Kinds by support condition (simply supported, cantilever, continuous), attributes (second moment of area, deflection) and two distinct bounds: bending stress for strength, serviceability for use. It is also the corpus case of a theory with a stated bound, since Euler-Bernoulli assumes small deflections.

New note: the cable, the tension-only member. Its shape is found rather than chosen: it takes the funicular of its loads, catenary under self weight and parabola under a uniform horizontal deck load, and the horizontal component of tension is constant along it. Three consequences worth keeping: sag sets the tension rather than decorating the form; transverse stiffness comes from geometry and pretension, not from material, so a slack cable is not stiff; and the structure must supply the compression the pull of the cable implies. Filed as the dual of the arch, same equilibrium with the sign reversed.

New note: the column, the member in axial compression whose characteristic failure is buckling rather than crushing. The Euler load pi^2 EI/L^2 makes the point in its exponents: capacity falls with the square of the length, so slenderness governs rather than area, and effective length rather than physical length is what enters. Three regimes — short crushes, long buckles elastically, intermediate does both and is empirical — and the stability bound is the shelf case where imperfections matter most, because the ideal formula is an upper bound.

New note: the structural connection, the joint that transmits action between members and the place where the strength of the structure is actually decided, since the shelf defines strength as the capacity of the weakest member or connection. Classified by mechanism of transmission — fused (weld), friction and bearing (bolt, rivet), contact (pin, bearing), anchorage into a substrate — each with its own characteristic failure. Two properties make it governing: the load path changes direction there, so combined actions meet; and it is the most redundant part of the structure, which is what lets a ductile joint redistribute and a brittle one fail progressively.
References now link Lamb's Hydrodynamics, the classical treatise behind the note's exact solutions and derivations.

New note: the foundation, the support through which a structure delivers its load to the ground — the one building block whose other half is a substance. Shallow (strip, pad, raft) and deep (pile, caisson) families, the joint quantities of the ground-foundation system (bearing pressure, settlement) and four bounds (bearing capacity, tolerable movement, sliding, overturning). Its most important statement is about which bound governs: foundations rarely break, they move, which is why the settlement bound — about use rather than survival — usually decides the size.

New note: the structural member, the building block structure.md names but had no note for. Typed as a Building Block specialized to Structural Member, and read as a body in its own right: the same steel section is a beam where it bends, a column where it is compressed and a tie where it hangs, so the member kinds are classified by the state of stress they are designed for rather than by shape. Six member kinds (bar, beam, column, cable, surface), the attributes that decide behaviour (cross-section, span) and the two bounds every member meets (strength, stability).

Open the Einstein field equations as a construction about a natural target: the law is a result, obtained by requiring the geometry side to be divergence-free (contracted Bianchi) and closed to a single admissible form by Lovelock's uniqueness theorem, while general relativity is the theory that carries it and the gravitational field is the segment of reality it represents. Types the root as an Epistemic Construction, kind Model; decomposes the Einstein tensor, the stress-energy source, the cosmological term, the metric field, the initial-value split, the Newtonian limit and the exact solutions; states the equivalence principle, the uniqueness requirement and the classical domain as the standards licensing the form; records the classical and strong-field tests and the singularity, cosmological-constant and quantum-gravity limits as the constraints the law carries inside itself; and evaluates it against the conceptuum criteria, where the weak verdicts are determinacy as a condition rather than a solution and adequacy as an effective rather than a fundamental law.

New note: capillary rise and depression as a competition between surface tension and adhesion, with the height inversely proportional to the passage radius — negligible in a bucket, dominant in a pore. Contact angle as the switch, Lucas-Washburn kinetics as the square-root-of-time front, and the phenomenon as a pump with no moving parts, which is why paper microfluidics works.

New note: cavitation — vapour bubbles from a pressure drop rather than a temperature rise, and the violence of their collapse, which concentrates the energy of the bubble volume into a point and erodes steel in water that never boiled. Inception as a pressure condition (cavitation number), nucleation sites as the reason clean liquids resist, and the double life of the phenomenon as damage mechanism and as tool.

New note: diffraction as the unavoidable consequence of a wave passing an aperture, and therefore the floor under every instrument's resolution. Fraunhofer and Fresnel regimes, the Rayleigh criterion, and the inversion that makes the same phenomenon an instrument — X-ray crystallography, electron diffraction, the grating.

New note: dispersion as the dependence of speed on frequency, with the two velocities it forces apart — phase and group — and the pulse broadening that follows from their difference. Material, waveguide and modal kinds; the zero-dispersion design as the case where two causes cancel; angular dispersion as the instrument.

New note: the Doppler effect, filed as a propagation phenomenon rather than a property of frequency. The note's content is the asymmetry the classical formula encodes — a moving source changes the wavelength in the medium, a moving observer only changes how often wavefronts are met, and in light the two are one case, which is where special relativity starts. Regimes: acoustic, relativistic, and the transverse term that has no classical analogue. Its sharpest section separates the effect from cosmological redshift, which looks like its recession term at low redshift and is a statement about the metric rather than about motion.
References: the laser Doppler vibrometer added beside radar, with the note that its shift is doubled by the return path.
Radar link repointed to the fisicatecnica radar note.

New note: interference as the visible content of superposition, and the argument that it belongs to neither wave alone — either wave gives a smooth intensity, only the pair gives structure. Mechanism through the path difference and the intensity law, with the fringe spacing as a ruler and visibility as the trace of coherence. Kinds: constructive, destructive, thin film; bounds: coherence and conservation of energy.

Move from nature/phenomena.md: the note becomes the master of a new phenomena shelf, holding the general phenomena that recur across sound, light and matter, and the note itself is rewritten from a two-quote definition into the family index with the typing and the membership table.

New note: the piezoelectric effect as one reversible coupling read in two directions, and the single structural condition that makes it exist at all — the absence of a centre of symmetry, which is why quartz has it and table salt does not. Direct and converse kinds, the resonator as the standard application, poling as the trick that gives a cheap ceramic the effect, and the Curie temperature as the operating bound.

New note: polarisation as the orientation of a transverse wave, and the observation that makes it a separate degree of freedom — two beams of orthogonal polarisation do not interfere. Kinds (linear, circular, birefringence), the states and their Stokes description, and the bounds: transversality as the test of the wave\'s nature, and Malus\'s law as the quantitative one.

New note: resonance, the phenomenon vibration.md lists as a bound and had no note for. The mechanism is a phase condition plus an energy balance, and its consequence is that amplitude at resonance is set by dissipation rather than by the drive — halve the damping and double the peak, remove it and there is no steady state. Kinds by domain (mechanical, acoustic, electrical), attributes (quality factor, bandwidth), bounds (dissipation, structural capacity).

Stub replaced with a full note. Ceramic defined by its processing contract rather than one chemistry: an inorganic, non-metallic body formed as clay or powder and consolidated by firing; the class boundary drawn against glass (amorphous, melt-formed), cement and plaster (hydrated at ambient temperature), metals (slip versus fracture), polymers and composites, with the property signature and its exceptions (ionic conduction, piezoelectricity, ferroelectricity, magnetism, superconductivity, transparency). The production chain is a five-stage table (body preparation, forming, drying, firing and sintering, glazing and finishing) with the techniques at each stage. The history runs from the fired-clay Venus of Dolni Vestonice through the East Asian earliest pottery (Xianrendong ~20,000 cal BP, Yuchanyan ~18,000-17,000), the Neolithic kiln and the Mesopotamian fast wheel, Egyptian faience and Chinese high-fired stoneware and porcelain, Islamic tin glaze and its European transmission, Meissen 1708 and Wedgwood, the nineteenth-century refractory and electrical-porcelain turn, and twentieth-century materials science (sintering theory, alumina and zirconia, SiC and Si3N4, glass-ceramics, bioceramics) to additive manufacturing. A ten-family table follows. References: an integrated chronological APA list of 28 works from Binns (1910) and Hobson (1915) to Rice (2015), no library entries created.

New stratum note: Grand Burgher (Grossbuerger, Grossbuergerrecht), the highest tier of urban citizenship in the German-speaking city-states of the Holy Roman Empire, from the Wikipedia article. The note works the legal order rather than the class: the three-tier hierarchy (hereditary grand burghers, petty burghers, non-burghers) into which the legally coequal burghers split before the fifteenth century; the privileges as Hamburg defined them (full unrestricted large-scale trade including foreign import and export, a bank account, eligibility for the Senate); the fees that made the order self-reproducing (50 Reichstaler against 7 in 1600, 758 Mark 8 Schilling against 46 in 1833); conferral by purchase, inheritance through male and female lines, and marriage; the abolition with the Weimar Constitution on 11 August 1919, with titles surviving only as family names, and the explicit point that the repeal did not touch the wealth or the firms. Typed Social Compound with the conferred status carried as a Social Property reading — the shelf's hardest case, since the rank is a threshold rather than a degree — and the ambiguity is stated as the concept's subject. 22-row decomposition, a 24-criterion conceptuum evaluation and verdict, and five QA entries (noble or not, why the right cost money, what 1919 abolished, whether the Hanseaten are the same thing, and the New Amsterdam 1657 borrowing).

New stratum note: the Hanseaten, the First Families of Hamburg, Bremen and Luebeck, from the Wikipedia article. The note is built on the paradox the sources state and the concept has to hold: a strictly republican oligarchy that banned the nobility from property, political life and residence inside Hamburg, then occupied the place nobles held elsewhere. Contents: the families as holders of hereditary grand burghership; the offices they held (mayor, senator, city diplomat, senior pastor); the family firm and the private bank; the endogamous marriage network and the unwanted traffic with the nobility; and the republican ethos — the honourable merchant, the hanseatic rejection of foreign honours, and the resistance to ennoblement, with the Berenberg-Gossler and Burchard anecdotes. Dated from about 1650 to 1918-19, with the point kept distinct: the constitutional order ended, the families did not. Boundary with Grand Burgher drawn explicitly in both notes — the right is the instrument, the Hanseaten are the formation that held it. 25-row decomposition, a 24-criterion evaluation whose verdict turns on the class's self-description, and five QA entries.

New stratum note: the intelligentsia, from the Wikipedia article. The note keeps the two national formations apart because the difference is the concept: the Polish inteligencja coined by Trentowski in the 1840s and given its programme by Libelt in 1844, and the Russian intelligentsiya as an oppositional order — Berlin's 'dedicated order, almost a secular priesthood' quoted — with the growth from 20,000 professionals in 1860 to 85,000 in 1900, Bulgakov on Peter the Great, the Narodniks and nihilists, the Bolshevik reading of a prosloyka without class character, the 1917 split and the Philosophers' steamers, the Soviet formalisation into scientific-technical and creative intelligentsia (engineering graduates 15,000 to 250,000, 1917-41), the post-Soviet decline, and the derived mass and free-floating intelligentsia. The boundary with the corpus's own Bildungsbuergertum is stated as functional rather than national: office and state service there, critique and the journal here. Lenin's polemic is carried in substance without its obscenity. 28-row decomposition, 24-criterion evaluation, six QA entries.

Typed as a Property at meso, with the secondary readings kept as prose (Phenomenon for the grouping pattern, Adaptation when heritable), and the boundary stated against Process, Natural System and the mere count of individuals — a crowd is not a society. The content is the four dimensions that separate one form from another (who associates, for how long, how work is divided, how association is recognised), and the two explanations that are complements rather than rivals: kin selection where relatedness is high and dispersal hard, mutual benefit and reciprocity among non-relatives. Forms from solitary through gregarious, colonial and eusocial to human ultrassociality; attributes of group size, relatedness, division of labour and recognition; bounds of resource base and disease transmission.

Move from nature/life/organism/sociality.md: physically moved into the social shelf, beside society.md, at the user's instruction. The propensity is still typed as a Property and the decomposition is unchanged; the tags now lead with social rather than nature.

Moved from social/meta/society.md into social/actor/collective/, where the genus notes of the collective shelf live. Society is the collective it describes, not a framework category, and the shelf now says so.

New note: sovereignty, filed beside the polity it is a property of rather than on the normative shelf, because sovereignty is carried by a polity and does not exist apart from it. Typed as `Social Property` (Ontic, read synontically where it depends on recognition) and explicitly not a kind of polity nor a part of one; distinguished from authority (the entitlement to decide inside the order) and legitimacy (the rightness of exercising it). Decomposition under three groupings: locus (personal, legal, parliamentary, popular, national), extension (territorial, economic, technological), the four classical marks (absoluteness, indivisibility, perpetuity, inalienability) each with its standing objection, and standing grades (full, pooled, bounded, absent) that restate as degrees what polity.md calls Dependent Standing. Then the theories table with what each cost, the limits that actually bind a sovereign, and the de jure / de facto and formal / substantive distinctions. The note says plainly that sovereignty is a claim treated as a fact, and that the vocabulary survives because it is what makes the violations legible.

New persona: Antonio Meucci, kept honest about the claim. Four columns of position — what the record supports and what it does not: that he transmitted speech is documentary rather than tested; that he was before Bell in date is not before him in law, since the 1871 caveat lapsed in 1874 for want of the fee; that the system failed him is true but the system was a fee-and-form regime, not a secret; and that the 2002 House resolution honoured his contribution without declaring him the inventor, whatever the retellings say. The sequence runs Havana, Staten Island, the caveat, its lapse, Bell's 1876 patent, and H.Res. 269 in 2002. The note exists for three reasons rather than the grievance: priority is procedural — a patent system rewards the maintenance of a claim, not the invention; symbolic correction changes memory and not the legal record; and the myth has a national function, saying more about the tellers than about the 1870s. Links the telecom technical decomposition, which is the corrective to reading an invention as a single moment.

New persona instance: Georgius Agricola (born Georg Bauer, 1494-1555), from the Wikipedia article and the corpus's own Agricola holdings. The note is written from his placement rather than from a biographical outline: a humanist who spent his working life in the mining towns of the Erzgebirge — town physician in Joachimsthal from 1527 and in Chemnitz from 1533, lord mayor of Chemnitz in 1546, 1547, 1551 and 1553, historiographer to Duke George — which is why his books came from the workings rather than from the library. New section 'The observation-based treatise' quotes the preface's evidential warrant verbatim (excluding what he had not himself seen or read or heard of), sets out the twelve books' scope, the woodcut machinery, fire-setting as a method described as already obsolete, the displacement of Pliny as the standard source with a two-century run, the German-glossary appendix and the words that survive from it (fluorspar, bismuth, basalt), and the 1912 Hoover translation. A nine-row Works table gives the attested titles with dates and what each is, with a note that the printing year of De ortu et causis subterraneorum is given as 1544 or 1546 and that the corpus's scientific-literature guide uses 1546. Two claims are kept at their real strength: the chymia naming is attributed to the sources rather than asserted, and the fossil error is stated plainly — the man usually called the father of mineralogy held that fossil shells were shaped by a materia pinguis fermented by heat rather than being the remains of living animals. The portrait is captioned as the fictive 1927 likeness it is. Section 'Place in the corpus' links the document the corpus actually holds (documents/books/agricola-1556-de-re-metallica.md, with its verified scans), the two historical-literature guides, the mechanical-system reading list, the mining system and sector, and mineral. New persona: Jost Bürgi (1552-1632), Swiss clockmaker, instrument maker and autodidact mathematician, at Kassel under Wilhelm IV and in Prague beside Kepler. The note holds two careers in one person: the cross-beat escapement and the remontoire, which made the clock accurate enough to time a star across a telescope crosshair and so turned it into a scientific instrument; and the mathematics — the Kunstweg sine iteration behind a lost Canon Sinuum that Kepler called the most precise known table, and a table of progressions built independently of Napier around 1600 and published only in 1620. The priority section records both verdicts without adopting either: Kepler's preface line about the "indolent man" who deserted his child at birth, and the conceptual counter-verdict that a table of antilogarithms is not a theory of the logarithm. References 1620 to 2016, including the Folkerts-Launert-Thom convergence proof.

New persona: Tertullian (c. 155 - c. 240), the first Christian author to write in Latin and the builder of the vocabulary Western theology argues in — trinitas, persona, substantia, sacramentum. The note separates three contributions: the apology (Apologeticus, c. 197, with the seed-of-the-martyrs sentence), the rule of faith (De praescriptione haereticorum, a procedural claim about the conditions under which an argument is possible rather than obscurantism), and the materialist psychology of De anima. It also records what he is remembered for wrongly: credo quia absurdum is a hostile paraphrase, and what he wrote in De carne Christi is narrower — credible because unfitting, certain because impossible — a claim about which criterion applies rather than a fideist slogan. Filed as the archetype of the polemic, which is now a glossarium term.

New note: the auction, on the coordinator shelf beside market-system.md — the structure note describes the market, this one describes a clearing procedure it can use. Filed outside market/instance/, which holds what is traded (financial, forex, housing, labour), because an auction is how trade is organised and cuts across all of them. The frame: a market whose clearing procedure is the product, which is why the rule is the whole subject. Forms table (English, Dutch, first-price, Vickrey, double, clock, reverse) and then the conflict that shapes the field — price discovery, efficient allocation and revenue cannot be served at once, and choosing among them is a decision taken once in the design and then out of politics. Theory that matters: revenue equivalence as a benchmark rather than a prediction, strategy-proofness in the second-price format and its rarity in practice, the winner's curse in common-value sales, and the recurring lesson that who shows up determines the result before the rule does. Cases: spectrum as the design field's laboratory, Treasury debt, Dutch auctions for perishables and their fit to spoilage, reverse auctions in procurement, clock auctions for carbon and electricity. Pathologies: auctioning to the extractor rather than the user, collusion, reserves as policy by stealth, and design capture by advisers.

New note on the interest rate — the concept money.md and state-finance.md both use and neither defined. Opens on the point that a rate is not a price: it needs a base, a period and a risk, and "the interest rate" in ordinary speech is several different objects. Composition table (real return, expected inflation, credit risk, maturity premium, liquidity premium) with the note that the components are inferred and never observed, so two economists can agree on the rate and disagree on its meaning. The family (policy, interbank, lending, bond yield, real) leading to the yield curve and the three readings that fit it. What it does: discounts the future, allocates over time, rations credit where it is capped, transmits policy, and becomes an instrument of the state in directed credit — the link to state capital allocation. Disputes: price versus administered number, negative real rates, the unobservable natural rate, and usury caps as distributional decisions made in moral language.

New note: imperialism, on the social-dynamic shelf beside globalization. It names the relation rather than the empire — the empires are filed as polities — and opens by admitting that the term is pejorative by construction: no state calls its own expansion imperialism, and a note that ignores the charge will misread half its sources. Readings kept as readings rather than competing types (relation of domination, process, regime, ideology, structure), then composition, six forms (colonial, informal free-trade, settler, protectorate, extractive enclave, cultural) and five theories stated with the objection each has to answer: Hobson, Lenin, Schumpeter, Gallagher and Robinson, Said. The point the table makes is that they are not rivals — two explain why the metropole wanted expansion, one how little formal control was needed, one the politics, one the categories. Closes on the five limits that actually ended empires: fiscal cost, military overstretch, legitimation at home, resistance in the periphery, rivalry between empires.

QA opened on the questions that define the note: imperialism where sovereignty is concentrated in a dictatorship, where the polity is internally divided, and where formal sovereignty and effective control diverge.

New note and a new logistics/ directory on the economic-activity shelf, beside trade/, production/ and interaction/: logistics is the activity family, and a hub is the node it is organised around. The note asks its own question in the front matter and answers it in the body — the economic function of a logistics hub, in five functions (consolidation and break-bulk, time and place utility, modal transshipment, value-added services, information and institutions), with the point made that a hub with only the first is a terminal rather than a hub. The role is then stated plainly: a hub does not merely move goods, it lowers the cost of distance and so rewrites the effective map of a region, which is why governments build them and why returns are so uneven. Typology table over seaport, airport, rail terminal, dry port, distribution centre and free zone, each with what it trades away; the three mechanisms connecting node to economy (agglomeration, gateway effects, routing power); and the limits — the enclave problem, the transshipment trap, subsidy races, and measurement by throughput, the flattering figure that rises regardless of who keeps the margin.

New note and a new `performance/` directory on the production shelf: the measures of what a production system achieves, as distinct from how it is organised (scheme/), how it changes (change/) or how it is represented (representation/). The note states the case that productivity falls short: productivity is output per unit of input inside a technique, so it is silent on whether the technique is the one worth using, and a system can maximise it inside one that is already obsolete. Competitiveness is the broader capacity to develop, adopt and deploy techniques — ordered with productivity rather than opposed to it, one measuring the return on a given way of doing things and the other whether the system can change the way it does them. Table of the two measures side by side (object, question, horizon, assumption, blind spot, failure mode), then the two consequences that earn the note: a productive system can be a failing one, and catching up is not the same as improving. Krugman's 1994 objection is answered rather than ignored — it lands against the market-share reading and much less well against the capability reading, which is not zero-sum and which his own alternative, productivity growth, cannot express. A closing note records that "competitivity" is not standard English and that the standard term is used, while the coinage is kept because it says the capacity more sharply than the worn-smooth standard word does.

New note: the fund of funds — a fund that selects managers rather than firms. Structure diagram, then what the second fee layer buys (manager selection, access, diversification, portfolio construction, monitoring, conditionality) and what it costs, with the honest test stated: whether the FoF fee is smaller than the cost of replicating its selection and monitoring internally, a calculation rarely done and rarely published. The conditionality function is singled out because it is the one that matters in development finance — a public purpose attached once at the FoF binds every fund beneath — and the two abuses are named: fee stacking without selection, and the insulation problem where the FoF report becomes the investor's only view of the portfolio.

New note: the mother fund — a public anchor that capitalises a family of daughter funds, sets their mandate and takes first-loss or subordinated risk so private co-investment happens. The note is explicit that its function is signalling and leverage rather than ownership: the public money is not the investment, it is what makes the investment happen. Structure diagram from state to mother fund to daughter funds to firms; a table of the five things it does that other instruments do not (anchoring, risk absorption, mandate setting, leverage, signalling); the three governance decisions that decide whether it works (what the mandate binds, how the anchor is priced, who selects the managers); and the two failure modes — subsidy disguised as investment, exposed by the counterfactual of how much private money would have come anyway, and mission drift, exposed by portfolio composition rather than return. Both are invisible in the two numbers usually reported, capital committed and capital deployed. Exemplars are marked as citations of the finance note rather than claims: whether any named institution is a mother fund is a question of mandate, not of name.

New note: state capital allocation, filed beside finance.md rather than in instrument/, because it is the decision that chooses among instruments and not an instrument itself — a state can hold every instrument in the space and still allocate badly. The spine: the state allocates capital with objectives that are not returns and with no single price to aggregate them, so the decision is political-administrative and its characteristic failures are political rather than computational. Allocation problem table (how much, to whom, on what terms, for what, for how long), the six criteria an allocation is judged on (market failure, additionality, leverage, capability, autonomy, fiscal cost) with the honest measure for each and the note that the criteria conflict — which is where allocations acquire their alibis. Four routes with their characteristic failure: direct/soft budget constraint, intermediated/mission drift, indirect/invisibility of tax expenditure and guarantees, portfolio/mandate displacement. Then the pathologies (picking winners as a failure to stop, capture, crowding out, flagship cycles, measurement by disbursement) and four instruments of discipline in ascending order of rarity: additionality testing, cost per outcome, composition reporting, sunset clauses.

New note: the Hong Kong Five-Year Plan, 2026–2030, on the framework shelf with the China, India, South Korea and Soviet plans. Filed as a Plan — the first round of a planning instrument in a polity whose doctrine was positive non-interventionism — with the instruction that one round is a plan, not yet an instrument, and the Strategic Planning Instrument reading kept as prose until renewal happens. Decomposition covers how it is published (full text, highlights/fact sheets, infographics and webcast), the seven parts, and the frames it inherits rather than creates (the Four Centres and talent hub from the national 14th plan, the national 15th plan that fixes the horizon, the Greater Bay Area outline). Then the institutional turn: an assigned national position, a land and housing programme too large for an annual budget cycle, and a standing integration commitment all pull toward a horizon longer than the fiscal year. The note refuses to reproduce figures it cannot check and instead names the three things that decide whether the plan is real: quantified targets, named machinery, and a second round.

New memorial essay: the Dominican scientific and technical documentation system. Its thesis is a distinction rather than a complaint — the country has a science system (Ley 139-01 of 2001: SNESCYT, MESCYT, FONDOCYT, with INDOTEC, IDIA and the Academia de Ciencias integrated at Art. 26) and no documentation system, so the memory of research is missing while the laboratory is not. Structured as seven questions, each answered: the problem, stated as five functions of which the country holds only the heritage halves; the scope, drawn by the rule harvest-do-not-build and by three things the system must refuse to become (a ranking agency, a second repository, a heritage digitisation programme); the incentive structure, which ties deposit to disbursement, funds the mandate with an overhead line, returns visibility to the depositor and penalises institutions rather than authors; the design and the run-time evaluations, with the metric that must not be the headline; five case studies (RCAAP, RECOLECTA, BDTD/Oasisbr, SNRD, ALICIA) and the history from the 1895 documentation movement and UNISIST 1971 through CONACITE 1983, the open-access turn and LAReferencia 2012 to the UNESCO recommendation of 2021.
Substantially rewritten and extended, 229 lines added and 112 removed: the essay reorganised with the documentary-system material developed in place rather than appended.

New note: the National Natural Science Foundation of China, filed under the chn research catalogue beside cas. The note is about the funding schema rather than the money. Four layers: nine discipline codes (A-H plus T for interdisciplinary), the project types from General Program and Key through Major Research Plans and the two non-consensual escape hatches to Joint Funds and the regional and international programmes; the talent ladder C-B-A with its former names, plus research groups and basic science centres; and the review, with the 2020 reviewer performance assessment and the rectification of string-pulling. The schema's consequences are stated as consequences: fields grow where panels are, people and projects are funded separately so the ladder shapes what the next proposal can promise, the label economy is intrinsic to any ladder that marks people (hence a renaming reform alongside a new continuation fund, two reforms in opposite directions), and the mission line is thin — Major Research Plans are a small share, so the national five-year plan does not travel through this instrument. The odds are given from the foundation's own numbers: about one in six across 2023, and 15.70% for the Young Scientists Fund C in chemical sciences in 2025. A set of papers closes the note, with the caveat that the figures are snapshots.

New note: the Swedish administrative system, filed with the polity rather than with the generic forms, which already carry the Swedish Government Agency as a kind. The argument is that the split between policy and delivery is not what makes the system distinctive — most states have one — but that the split is constitutional: the Instrument of Government forbids ministerial rule, a minister may not decide how an agency decides a particular case, and decisions are taken by the government collectively. Structure table (Riksdag, government, ministries, agencies, oversight) with what each may and may not do; then the two supporting institutions that make independence work rather than merely exist — the principle of public access since 1766, and review on legality through the administrative courts and the ombudsmen. The costs are stated plainly: nobody below the government can reconcile two agencies that disagree, ministerial accountability is real but diffused, and the model assumes a small high-capacity civil service and a culture of collective decision. Compared against the UK executive agency (insulation in a framework document) and the Japanese incorporated administrative agency (insulation in incorporation): the Swedish form puts it in the constitution.

The note now says how the system is steered, not only how it is divided. Formulation written. The type is settled as Social Relation — the recognized standing of a holder over an object against the duty-bearers, read as Ontic where it is enforced and Synontic where its content exists through recognition — and the recursive decomposition added: the four incidents (claim right, liberty, power, immunity), the holder kinds, the specified and unspecified duty-bearers that separate property from contract, the object kinds including the virtual object, the title forms from ownership to security interest, the five property regimes, and the four attributes of exclusivity, transferability, divisibility and duration. The two remaining Formulation questions filled. New note: Romanitas, on the ideational shelf as a civilizational worldview and catalogued in the ideational family table beside Civilization. Opens with the word's provenance — attested in Tertullian, a Carthaginian provincial writing around 210, and rare in Latin, which prefers humanitas, civilitas, mos maiorum, urbanitas — and makes that the problem: the name for Roman-ness was coined at the edge of the empire. Content decomposed into Latinity, ius, civitas, mos maiorum, humanitas, cultus and urbanitas; phases from the city through the Christian empire to Byzantine Romania; associated with Hellenism, Christianity and imperial ideology. Then the extension mechanism (grants of citizenship to 212, the army, the colony, the co-optation of provincial elites, the common law), the history of the standard and the membership, and the critique: an elite construction, the legitimation half of empire, and a modern word for a Roman absence given the revisionist case against Romanisation since the 1990s.

New technical note: the Product Requirements Document, from the Wikipedia article, in the technica shell with the four Formulation questions and a 24-row instance decomposition. Typed Technical Specification as its primary kind, with the argument turning on exclusion: the guide’s Technical Blueprint is a description that prescribes how to create an artifact, and the PRD is the artifact that refuses to prescribe, so its own rule disqualifies the blueprint reading — the note is typed by its prohibition as well as by its content. Readable secondarily as a Technical Element Set (the requirements-document family) and as a blueprint only in the degenerate case where the document has swallowed the design, which the note keeps as the concept’s characteristic failure. Contents: the requirements chain (user or client or marketing → PRD, or MRD when marketing authors it → analysis by the maker → functional specification or technical requirements document); the two regimes the article names (cascading, where the requirements are fixed in their entirety before work, and agile, where they are framed at a high level for prioritisation and elaborated per cycle — a change of granularity, not of existence); the component list as a template for a class rather than a definition, with the article’s own caveat that non-software PRDs drop the software-specific elements and add their own; and the failure modes (user misunderstanding, incomplete or inaccurate information, unclear communication, unrealistic timeframes) against the three problems it is claimed to prevent (architecture mismatch, overlooked dependencies, underestimated complexity). The note records that the article marks its two load-bearing claims — the what-not-how rule and the component list — as uncited, and states them as the article’s formulation rather than as settled doctrine. Evaluation: strong on identification, discriminative power, performative effects and purpose adequacy; weak on definitional clarity, temporal stability and misuse resistance, with the verdict that the concept describes a role in a development regime more reliably than it describes a text. Five QA entries (is it a specification, why it must not say how, against the MRD, against agile, technical element against management artifact).

New note on the wireless communication system as a technical element: the full chain from source to sink, plus the two coordination layers a cable does not need — duplexing and medium access — on the argument that the system is defined by the absence of a guided medium, and that every decision in it answers that absence. Architecture table with the wireless-specific problem at each stage, then transmission (electromagnetic waves, modulation, and the three physical resources plus Shannon's limit). The historical developments table is the note's centre and now carries the patents: Marconi UK 12039 of 1896 as the first radio patent, Tesla 1900, de Forest's audion 1907, the transistor patents of 1950, Kilby and Noyce on the integrated circuit in 1959, Cooper's radio telephone system patent of 1975. The table is read in three waves — physics and patent, then components, then systems — with the observation that each wave was financed by a claim to exclusivity and that the priority disputes are as much part of the history as the circuits. A generations table (1G to 5G by multiple access) and a relation table close it.

History: the claims that lost added, with their patents. Drawbaugh (application 1880, Telephone Cases 1888) as the claimant whose conception was held not to be reduction to practice; Landell de Moura with Brazilian patent 3,279 and the three U.S. patents of 1904 (771,917 Wave Transmitter, 775,337 Wireless Telephone, 775,846 Wireless Telegraph, on applications filed 1901-02, after public demonstrations in 1899-1900); and Armstrong and Orling with the British patents of 1899, 1900 and 1903 and the U.S. Aerophone patent 744,001, whose claim was conduction through earth and water rather than radiation. A new passage states what the four rows have in common — the filter is not physics but reduction to practice, disclosure in the form the office recognises, the fee that keeps a claim alive, and the capital behind it — and links the Meucci persona as the same filter seen from the wire side.

The Landell de Moura row corrected on two points and given its comparison. The year is 1900, not 1899-1900, and the patent is named properly as Brazilian Patent No. 3,279. More importantly the claim is now stated correctly: June 1900 is six months before Fessenden's December transmission, so he is first by date and second by record — a new paragraph separates the three firsts that get collapsed (Bell's speech on light in 1880, Landell's radio voice in June 1900, Fessenden's in December 1900) and names the asymmetry: his demonstration is documented by the press rather than by a published test anyone could reproduce, which is why the standard account omits him. The earlier "early, not first" wording was simply wrong about the chronology.

New practice note: nanomedicine as the chain that gives a therapeutic or diagnostic agent a nanoscale carrier or form and carries it to regulatory acceptance. Typed as Technical Practice, readable as Technical Element Set, with the purposes, problems, constraints, tasks, general and constitutive techniques, carrier platforms (liposome, lipid nanoparticle, polymeric nanoparticle and micelle, inorganic particle, nanocrystal, antibody-drug conjugate), delivered medicines, characterisation instruments, standards and evaluations; adds the platform, application and manufacturing tables and the conceptuum evaluation of the 1-100 nm convention.

New practice note: reliability engineering as the practice that prevents, finds, tolerates and estimates failure over a stated life. Typed as Technical Practice, readable as Technical Element Set, with the purposes (prevent, correct, tolerate, estimate), the problems (random, wear-out, common cause, latent, human error), the tasks, the general techniques (FMEA/FMECA, FTA, RBD, life-data and Weibull analysis, accelerated life testing, derating, redundancy, RCM, FRACAS), the constitutive techniques, the test facilities, the IEC and MIL standards, the agent, the constraints and the verification/validation pair. Adds the measures table (R(t), failure rate, MTTF/MTBF, availability, maintainability, mission and basic reliability) with the bathtub caution, the failure-regime table, the analysis-technique table, the requirements-and-programme section and the reliability/quality/safety boundary, plus the conceptuum evaluation.

New technical domain: Separation Science and Technology, a shallow domain set in the corpus's Technical Element Set idiom (the Geological Resource Development and Food Production pattern): three blockquotes (definition, complement-of-the-observation, the cut), the three Formulation questions, one Instance Tree Path table, and References. The root is declared Technical Element Set and carries ten direct sub-domain constituents — solvent extraction, ion exchange and sorption, membranes, distillation and evaporation, crystallization and precipitation, chromatography, filtration and mechanical separation, flotation, gas separation, and electrochemical/electromembrane separation — over the flat spine (Technical Evolution, Technical Purpose, Technical Domain Reality Model, Technical Requirement, Technical Standard), 36 rows in all, no member re-decomposed. Three judgements are recorded rather than smoothed over. The name: the field's own name carries a science whose inquiry half is epistemic and belongs to Chemical Engineering and the chemical sciences, while the set composes only the techniques that realize a separation, and the note says so. The boundary: mineral beneficiation is deliberately not a member because it is the application of this family, already carried inside Geological Resource Development as its Beneficiation And Processing Set; chemical reaction is excluded because a reactor transforms a substance while a separator only redistributes it, and where a reaction is the instrument (precipitation, electrodeposition) the separation is the end. The state of the members: no member has a note, the corpus's only separation material is two natural stubs (Separation Process and Chromatography, both undecomposed) plus the discipline note that names separation as a plant question without decomposing it, and the depth the corpus does have is bench-scale and one system at a time — recorded as a Member Coverage Requirement in the spine rather than presented as an even frontage. The reality model carries the domain's real constraint: a separator redistributes matter and cannot change the elements it separates, so mass balance and the energy/entropy floor bound every member; chemical similarity is the axis of difficulty. The Technical Evolution spine runs fire assay and parting → distillation → industrial extraction of the 1940s → sorption and membranes → simulation and energy integration → the data-driven discovery era, whose instances are the four papers added with this note. References integrated into one list (guide, sibling domains, knowledge, natural stubs, application, bench cases).

New technica note: the laser Doppler vibrometer, filed beside radar on the industry shelf and typed the same way — a Production Technical Object, a produced electromagnetic measurement instrument rather than a production plant. The note is organised around the three details that make the instrument what it is: the factor of two (the beam goes to the surface and back, so the shift is 2v/lambda and the output is velocity directly), heterodyne detection with a Bragg cell (without the carrier a fringe-counting system measures speed but not sign), and speckle (the surface is rarely a mirror, which is why retroreflective tape is part of the method). The instance tree decomposes the assembly, the configuration that decides validity (stand-off and focus, velocity range, surface treatment), the instrument kinds by function (single-point, scanning, three-dimensional, differential) and the evaluations that bound it: line-of-sight constraint, speckle dropout, and calibration traceability through the wavelength rather than a shaker.

New technica note: the truck, filed on the industry shelf and typed as a Production Technical Object inside the transportation-vehicles system. The note is built on the three numbers set outside the engineering — axle load, gross weight and dimensions, and duty cycle — and on the one that explains the axle limit: pavement damage scales with roughly the fourth power of axle mass, which is why a heavy vehicle has many axles rather than one strong one. Payload is named as the design variable, which is where electrification bites: a battery is mass that earns nothing, and whether the trade closes is a question about the duty cycle, not about the vehicle. It also records the modular cut (a rigid truck and a tractor-trailer are one architecture in two products, because length limits count the trailer) and the evaluations that bound the object, including driver hours, which no design can remove. The instance tree covers ten constituents, five kinds, four configuration values and four evaluations.

Thirty-six are added: boulanger, charcutier, poissonnier, patissier, rotisseur, raffineur de sucre, distillateur liquoriste, savonnier, vigneron and jardinier into Cibaria; macon, charpentier, couvreur, vitrier, plombier and miroitier into Architectura; charron, sellier and marechal into Transportaria; gantier into Coriaria; passementier, bonneterie, blanchisseur and foulon into Textilis; tourneur, fondeur, fil d archal and fabricant d ancres into Mechanica; parcheminier and cartonnier into Papyrologica; relieur into Typographica; mercier and perruquier into Manufactura; cordier into Funalis; boyaudier into Acustica; and charbonnier into Silvicultura. Individual authors are named where they are documented (Malouin for the boulanger, Duhamel for the couvreur and the charbonnier, Lalande for the parcheminier, Doublette Desbois for the vitrier, Demachy for the distillateur, Reaumur and Duhamel for the ancres); elsewhere the Academie is recorded as the corporate author. The guide now carries 1,373 rows.

New guide: the venues rather than the works. Twelve Logia sections — the academy proceedings, mathematics, physics, astronomy, chemistry, earth sciences, life sciences, medicine, psychology, engineering, economics, and the electronic era — each a table of journals with founding year, body and what the venue is known for. The framing is the journal as an institution with four functions (registration, certification, dissemination, archiving) and the story of those functions separating: the academies did registration and archiving for a century before refereeing existed, and the preprint server has now taken registration and dissemination back. The Comptes rendus page is cited in the academy section and in the references, as the venue behind the integral-operator citations.

New guide: the study of the history of technology, as a field rather than as another catalogue. Its organising distinction is that the history of science studies what was known and its evidence is mostly text, while the history of technology studies what was made and its evidence is mostly not text — an asymmetry that makes the field methodologically distinct rather than a branch of history with odd sources. Sections: the four objects a technical history can be about (artefact, technique, system, knowledge), since a note that cannot say which will drift between them; the evidence problem as a table of what each kind establishes and cannot establish, including experimental reconstruction, the field's most distinctive and most dangerous method; the interpretive traditions read as positions to be declared (technological determinism, Mumford's cultural critique, social construction, systems, evolution); a six-step method for writing a technical history in this corpus, which amounts to decomposing the artefact with the technica grammar and dating the change rather than the period; and the shelf of works.
